September isn't the latest figure, and multiplying it by 12 would give a wrong answer.

- **September isn't the latest.** October 2026 was released on 2026-11-18 and is the latest month.
- **The figure is already annual.** Table 34-10-0158-01 reports housing starts as a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR). That rate is the monthly pace scaled up to a full year. Multiplying by 12 counts each year twelve times over.

| Month | SAAR (units) |
|---|---|
| October 2026 | 244,558 |
| September 2026 | 250,072 |

- **What the annual pace means:** September's pace is about 250,072 homes a year, and October's is about 244,558.
- **What your multiplication gives:** 250,072 × 12 = 3,000,864. That is roughly 12 times any realistic annual total, so I wouldn't use it.
- **Limits of the estimate:** A SAAR is a pace for one month, not a forecast of the year's total. I haven't checked actual year-to-date starts, which come from the unadjusted series.

I couldn't check this against CMHC's published methodology. None of the tools I have covers CMHC documentation, so this answer comes from memory and the wording may differ from CMHC's.

- **Absorbed:** CMHC's Market Absorption Survey follows newly completed units, which are units in structures that have just finished construction. It counts a unit as absorbed once it has been sold (for ownership units) or rented (for rental units). Before that, the unit is counted as unabsorbed inventory.
- **Sold:** As I remember it, CMHC treats a unit as sold when a binding sales contract exists, meaning the purchaser has signed and made a deposit. The buyer does not have to have moved in, and the sale does not have to have closed. I'm not certain of CMHC's exact wording on this.

Check the definitions in CMHC's Housing Market Information Portal, or in the methodology notes for the Starts and Completions Survey and the Market Absorption Survey, before you cite this.

I couldn't check this against CMHC's methodology page. The tools I searched had no CMHC Rental Market Survey documentation, so this comes from my own knowledge of CMHC's published methodology.

- **When:** CMHC conducts the survey every year in October. It publishes the results in December, and I believe that is a December release in the same year.
- **What it covers:** The survey covers privately initiated, purpose-built rental structures. These are apartment buildings and row (townhouse) structures with at least three rental units. It covers urban centres with a population of 10,000 or more.
- **What it leaves out:** The survey doesn't cover condominium units rented out by their owners, secondary rental such as basement suites and single-family homes, or collective dwellings. I'm less sure of this list than of the rest.
